name: Mike Rutenberg

views.text: Style beats scheme: effort, speed and playing for each other matter more than any call sheet.
When you inherit a great defense, build on what already works instead of tearing it up.
Character comes first; how a player lives off the field shows up on it.
A defense should celebrate its plays; confidence and energy are part of the plan.
Disguise only works if the communication behind it is perfect.
A new coordinator owes his stars a conversation before he owes them a plan.
Honest self-scouting by the staff is the first step out of any slump.

signatures: connects young players with greats of their position
keeps in touch with players he coached years earlier and recruits them to follow him
talks about his inherited defense with respect before describing changes

motivation.want: to keep a top defense elite and step out of a famous shadow
motivation.fear: that any drop in the defense gets pinned on him

voice: Energetic and warm, with a teacher's habit of explaining the why; he talks about style, effort and character more than fronts and coverages. Respectful of what he inherited and of veteran players, candid about self-evaluation, and openly excited about the job.

evidence.summary: OTA notebook as Jets linebackers coach: praises a new signing's familiarity with Saleh's system, energy and toughness, Quincy Williams' speed and strength, and C.J. Mosley's mind and leadership. Shows how he talks about players; little on method.

Hire report: 44, Cornell graduate and D.C. native; began as a Washington personnel intern and assistant to Joe Gibbs, then UCLA, New Mexico State, the Jaguars (2013-19), the 49ers (2020), four seasons as Jets linebackers coach and one as Falcons pass game coordinator. First DC job, replacing Schwartz on a top-ranked defense whose scheme Monken does not plan to change.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Browns On SI), Nick Pedone
evidence.summary: Introduction: he will build on what players and coaches already do well; wants a defense that plays hard, fast, violent and smart, with energy and celebration; stresses style over scheme; promises honest self-evaluation; kept most of the defensive staff; eager to meet and learn from the star pass rusher. Reported remarks.
Short report on the introduction, headlined on his saying he is beyond fired up; notes he has big shoes to fill after Schwartz. Little beyond the headline.

Quincy Williams on signing in Cleveland: calls Rutenberg a close mentor, like a brother, who coached him in Jacksonville and New York; says he puts character before football, wants players to be themselves, and taught him nearly everything he knows at linebacker, from zone freedom to eye discipline and preparation habits. One player's warm testimony.

Camp notes: a safety calls the new scheme exotic, with heavy disguise and communication, while the Schwartz foundation stays; a second-year linebacker says Rutenberg connected him with Luke Kuechly, his childhood idol. Brief items.
